test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On 11 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

As good as gold

options.text: A person who is obedient and well-behaved
A person who is good like gold but not better

solution:
The correct answer is '**A person who is obedient and well-behaved**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom '**As good as gold**' is '**A person who is obedient and well-behaved**'.
 
• **As good as gold**: (especially of a child) very well behaved.
 
 
• E.g.: *The children were **as good as gold**, waiting patiently at the entrance*.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at some behavior-related idioms.
 
 
• **Turn over a new leaf**- to start behaving in a better way:

 
 
• For example: Billy decided to *turn over a new leaf *and stop teasing his younger brother.
 
 
 
• **Take stock**- make an overall assessment of a particular situation, typically before making a decision.
 
 
• For example: Ka-yan spent the night before her birthday* taking stock *of all she had achieved so far.
 
 
 
• **Kick the habit**- to give up something harmful that you have done for a long time:
 
 
• For example: Sandy has bitten his nails for years, but he really wants to *kick the habit*.
